key: series:1/series_description
    // Please describe the experimental series - what is done, with what aim, and where its record comes from (leave empty to skip)?
    // source: C: suggested by Claude Code from the setup sheet, adapted by Laura Fadler (04.10.2026)
Batch hydrogenation of adiponitrile (RDY) towards hexamethylenediamine over a platinum catalyst in water and isopropanol, in the stirred, cooled reactor vessel001 of Lab 109: hydrogen sparged at controlled pressure, the temperature controlled, pressure, temperature and hydrogen uptake logged, the final reaction mixture analysed by GC. Recorded by hand and in the logged data of the reactor - there is no ELN record.

key: series:1/task:for-Mass_Molecule_0007_Phase_LiquidVessel_Phase_Evidence_1_ExperimentSpecific/description
    // [hlo:SeriesSpecific] Please describe Analysing the final reaction mixture by GC (optional, leave empty to skip)?
    // source: C: entered by Laura Fadler (partly suggested by Claude Code) before source lines were kept (rule 2.10, 29.09.2026); answer file up to 01.10.2026 in answers_archive/hydrogenation_answers_20261001_before_sources.txt
Gas chromatography of the final reaction mixture. One injection, one chromatogram: the adiponitrile left over, the hexamethylenediamine formed and the dimeric by-product are read off it as three separate peaks, which is why this is one measurement with three results rather than three measurements.

key: series:1/task:for-Volume_Material_Sample_In_Syringe_Reference_1_ExperimentSpecific/description
    // [hlo:SeriesSpecific] Please describe Assuming the sample volume (required: what is assumed, and why it may be assumed)?
    // source: C: entered by Laura Fadler (partly suggested by Claude Code) before source lines were kept (rule 2.10, 29.09.2026); answer file up to 01.10.2026 in answers_archive/hydrogenation_answers_20261001_before_sources.txt
The volume drawn with the syringe and pushed into the GC vial is taken as 1 mL: the syringe holds 1 mL, and a GC vial holds 1.5-2 mL and is usually filled with about 1 mL. The volume actually drawn was not recorded.

A syringe takes about 1 mL of the reaction mixture out of the vessel after the run and transfers it into a GC vial. Drawn before the vessel is emptied - afterwards the liquid is already outside the system and cannot be sampled any more.

    // [hlo:ExperimentSpecific] Please describe Watching the material go in and out (optional, leave empty to skip)?
    // source: C: entered by Laura Fadler (partly suggested by Claude Code) before source lines were kept (rule 2.10, 29.09.2026); answer file up to 01.10.2026 in answers_archive/hydrogenation_answers_20261001_before_sources.txt

key: series:1/experiment:1/task:for-Transfer_Nitrogen-GasExchange-from-L109_Air_GasPhase-to-GasVessel_Phase_PhasePairInterface_Phase_GasVessel_Phase_L109_Air_GasPhase_Occurrence_Reference_1_ExperimentSpecific/description
    // [hlo:ExperimentSpecific] Please describe Assuming room air enters the headspace while the vessel is open (required: what is assumed, and why it may be assumed)?
    // source: C: the reactor is assumed open while it is filled - room air enters the headspace (decided by Laura Fadler on 01.10.2026)
Not observed, a modelling choice for this example: while the vessel is open for charging (see 'Assuming when the vessel and the vial were open'), nitrogen and oxygen of the room air are assumed to enter the headspace. The real experiment may have purged the headspace with hydrogen; modelling that would need a purging step in the procedure.

    // [hlo:ExperimentSpecific] Please describe Watching the material go in and out (optional, leave empty to skip)?
    // source: C: entered by Laura Fadler (partly suggested by Claude Code) before source lines were kept (rule 2.10, 29.09.2026); answer file up to 01.10.2026 in answers_archive/hydrogenation_answers_20261001_before_sources.txt

Assuming room air enters the headspace while the vessel is open

key: series:1/experiment:2/task:for-Transfer_Nitrogen-GasExchange-from-L109_Air_GasPhase-to-GasVessel_Phase_PhasePairInterface_Phase_GasVessel_Phase_L109_Air_GasPhase_Occurrence_Reference_1_ExperimentSpecific/description
    // [hlo:ExperimentSpecific] Please describe Assuming room air enters the headspace while the vessel is open (required: what is assumed, and why it may be assumed)?
    // source: C: the reactor is assumed open while it is filled - room air enters the headspace (decided by Laura Fadler on 01.10.2026)
Not observed, a modelling choice for this example: while the vessel is open for charging (see 'Assuming when the vessel and the vial were open'), nitrogen and oxygen of the room air are assumed to enter the headspace. The real experiment may have purged the headspace with hydrogen; modelling that would need a purging step in the procedure.
